events.text:
[IT Help chat · signed in as Brenda Walsh (E2901) · ticket T-6009]
hi, my phone says my work account is locked?? I can still use my computer but email on my phone won't work. can you unlock it please

args.summary: Possible account compromise for brenda.walsh (E2901). The account is locked for too many failed sign-ins. Between 07:05 and 09:40 PT today there were 11 failed sign-ins from Bucharest, Romania; her earlier sign-in history shows only Portland, US. A new MFA device ("Android device", MD-2901-2) was also registered by self-service today at 08:02 PT; we haven't yet asked the employee if she added it. She contacted the desk (ticket T-6009) asking for an unlock because email on her phone stopped working. No unlock, reset or MFA change has been done.

args.note: Unlock requested. Account shows 11 failed sign-ins today from Bucharest, RO (new country), plus an MFA device registered today at 08:02. This is a compromise indicator, so escalated to Security on-call. No unlock or other account changes made.

events.text:
Hi Brenda, I looked at your account and I can't unlock it right now. The lock came from 11 failed sign-in attempts this morning, between about 7:05 and 9:40 AM PT. All of them came from Bucharest, Romania, but your account has only ever signed in from Portland. That pattern could mean someone else is trying to get into your account. When that happens, I have to pass it to our Security team and leave the account as it is.

What I've done:
- **Sent this to Security on-call** (reference SEC-500). They usually respond within an hour, and they'll contact you to check the account and get you back in safely.
- **Marked your ticket T-6009 as escalated.**

Until they reach you:
- Please don't approve any sign-in or MFA prompts you didn't start yourself.
- A new authenticator device called "Android device" was added to your account today at 8:02 AM. Did you set that up? Please tell me or Security either way, because it helps them a lot.
- Your computer still working is fine. Just don't try to sign in again on your phone yet.

Sorry about the hassle with your phone email. This is to keep your account safe.

Oh no, Bucharest? I've never been there, I've been in Portland all week. So that's not me.

I did get a couple of odd sign-in prompts on my phone this morning and I tapped deny on them. I didn't add any new phone or device, though. I only use my Pixel 8 for the authenticator. So I definitely didn't set up any "Android device."

Please tell Security I'm worried and happy to help however they need. Should I change my password now, or wait for them to contact me?

args.summary: Update to SEC-500 (ticket T-6009): Brenda Walsh says she has been in Portland all week and the Bucharest sign-ins were not her. She did NOT add the "Android device" MFA authenticator (MD-2901-2, registered today 08:02 PT); her only device is her Pixel 8. She got several unexpected sign-in prompts this morning and denied them. She's worried, will help however needed, and is waiting for Security's guidance before changing her password.

events.text:
Thanks, Brenda. That helps a lot. I've sent Security an update (reference SEC-501). I told them:
- You've been in Portland all week, so the Bucharest sign-ins weren't you.
- You didn't add the "Android device." You only use your Pixel 8.
- You denied the strange sign-in prompts this morning.
- You're worried and happy to help however they need.

Denying those prompts was exactly the right thing to do.

**On your password, please wait for Security.** Because someone added a device to your account, they'll want to handle it all together: remove the device you didn't add, reset your password and check your account. If you change things before then, it could get in their way or alert whoever is trying to get in. They usually respond within an hour.

Until they contact you:
- Keep denying any sign-in or MFA prompts you didn't start.
- Don't type your password into any links you get by email or text, even if they look like they come from IT. Security will reach you directly.
- Your computer is fine to keep using.

Your ticket T-6009 stays escalated to Security. Sorry this happened. You've done everything right.

Okay, thanks for passing that on. I'll wait for Security and won't change my password yet.

Quick question while I have you: should I keep my phone on and near me in case they call, or is there a number I should watch for?

args.query: Security on-call contact employee after account compromise

articles.title: Resetting your password
articles.body: If you're locked out or your password expired, message IT Help. We'll verify your identity (see the IT policy) and send a one-time reset link to the mobile number or personal email on your HR record.

articles.title: New phone? Moving your MFA
articles.body: If you still have your old phone, add the new device in Settings > Security, then remove the old one. If you've lost your phone, message IT Help for an MFA reset; you'll need to verify your identity.

articles.title: Software licenses
articles.body: Licenses are assigned by IT Help after manager approval. Seat counts are fixed by our contracts; when a product is full, IT Help can raise a purchase request.

events.text:
Yes, please keep your phone on and nearby. I don't have a specific phone number to give you, and I couldn't find one in our help articles, so I don't want to guess. Security may call you, message you here in the workplace chat, or email your work address. You can use your computer normally in the meantime.

To stay safe while you wait:
- **Genuine Security staff will never ask for your password or MFA codes,** and they won't ask you to approve a sign-in prompt. If anyone does, it isn't Security.
- If a call seems suspicious, hang up and message IT Help here. You can quote your references (SEC-500 / SEC-501, ticket T-6009) and we'll check whether it was really them.
- Keep denying any sign-in prompts you didn't start.

If you haven't heard from anyone in about an hour, message us here and we'll follow up.
Thanks, that's really helpful. I'll keep my phone on and nearby, and I'll message you here if I haven't heard from anyone in about an hour. I really appreciate you looking into this so quickly.

You're welcome, Brenda. You spotted something wasn't right, denied the strange prompts and reported it quickly, which is exactly what you should do.

Security has your case (SEC-500 / SEC-501), and your ticket T-6009 will stay escalated until they've sorted it out. Message us here anytime if you need anything else. Hope your phone email is back soon.
